summary: Proxy-injected Proxy-Authorization header causing 403s on artifact fetch and streaming for Private deployment
description: Issue summary: Verdant Health reports intermittent 403 responses and aborted streaming when private deployment nodes attempt to download model artifacts and when customer-facing streaming requests go through their corporate TLS inspection appliance. Impact: model pulls fail (~15% of attempts) and streaming calls frequently abort mid-response causing application errors for end users. Environment: private deployment in customer VPC peered to Redwood control plane; customer uses inline TLS inspection (corporate proxy) that terminates and re-establishes TLS.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Place a VM inside customer's private VPC that uses the corporate TLS inspection appliance for egress.
2) Attempt to curl a Redwood presigned artifact URL from the VM: curl -v -H "Range: bytes=0-" "<presigned-url>"
3) Observe HTTP/403 responses intermittently and check returned headers.
4) Initiate a streaming completion request from an app behind the same TLS inspection appliance and observe aborted streams / early EOFs.
logs: Control plane log excerpt (artifact-fetch): GET /artifact/pull?object=llama-3-70b 403 X-Request-ID=4d2f: error="invalid-auth-header" details="Proxy-Authorization header present"
Packet capture (tcpdump) from customer egress shows injected header: Proxy-Authorization: Basic ZGVtbzpwYXNzd29yZA==
Edge nginx access log (streaming endpoint): client=10.2.3.45 - - "POST /v1/streams HTTP/2.0" 499 - "-" "Proxy-Authorization: Basic ..."
Application error sample: streaming aborted: io.EOF after 3.1s, underlying status: UNAUTHENTICATED (code 16)
investigation: Support reproduced 403s by proxying requests through customer's TLS inspection appliance in their staging environment; observed Proxy-Authorization header injected on outgoing connections.

Control plane has a defensive header validation that rejects incoming requests containing Authorization-like headers when authentication is via signed presigned URLs; this is triggering 403s when the Proxy-Authorization header is present.

Tcpdump and proxy logs show the appliance rewrites SNI to an internal inspection hostname and injects Proxy-Authorization for its own backend auth; the presigned URL validation on Redwood treats the extra header as an authentication attempt and fails validation.

Streaming aborts appear correlated to header injection + TLS re-termination causing HTTP/2 connection reuse to fail (proxy reuses connection for multiple streams and inserts auth header intermittently).
comments: Morgan Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial intake from Verdant Health. They saw 403s for artifact fetches and aborted streams since 2026-03-08; provided sample presigned URL and packet captures.

Verdant Health (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed corporate TLS inspection is handled by SecureGate v3; they have a policy that injects Proxy-Authorization for backend chaining. They can add rewrite rules but asked if Redwood can tolerate the header.

Ravi Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally by standing up SecureGate in lab. Confirmed Proxy-Authorization header present and control plane code path returns 403 with reason 'invalid-auth-header'.

Elena Ruiz (Product) 2026-03-13: Requested impact numbers and whether this can be safely stripped at ingress; noted potential risk if proxies inject arbitrary auth headers and how that interacts with presigned URLs and mTLS.

Verdant Health 2026-03-14: Willing to add a temporary rewrite rule to remove Proxy-Authorization from egress to Redwood if we provide recommended header filters. Asked for guidance and a patch timeline.
resolution: Workaround (customer): Verdant Health to add a reverse proxy rule to strip Proxy-Authorization for traffic destined to Redwood control plane and S3-compatible artifact endpoints.

Short-term product mitigation (planned): Add ingress header sanitization that drops Proxy-Authorization / Proxy-Authenticate / X-Proxy-Auth headers for requests authenticated via presigned URLs. Target patch: 2026-03-20 for staging rollout.

Long-term: Update docs and private deployment checklist to call out proxies that inject auth headers and include recommended proxy rewrite rules. Add a flag in Private control-plane config to toggle aggressive header stripping for customers that request it.

Post-incident: Create an internal runbook for diagnosing header-injection issues (linked in related_confluence_pages) and add automated checks in onboarding that detect injected auth headers during test artifact pulls.
